comment: D65/D69: the pinned C toolchain native build scripts run with (clang, libclang, llvm-ar), the LLVM project's own release of the LLVM version llvm.json pins (23.1.4) until our fork's archive carries a clang (.github/scripts/llvm.py). Read by blaze_build_script::native::pin. `sysroots`: the C library headers per target; macOS takes the machine's SDK by version and the headers read (D69), Linux a pinned glibc sysroot: none pinned yet (null).
host_tools_comment: D71: the only programs other than the C toolchain a native build script may start, per host target. `names`: the tools, space-separated, sorted. Per tool: `path`, the resolved real path (no link), granted read and execute; `reads`, space-separated folders its runtime needs, granted read-only (perl: libperl.dylib, privlib and archlib are /System/Library/Perl/<v>, vendorlib /System/Library/Perl/Extras/<v>, from libperl's own Config.pm; the site folder /Library/Perl is NOT granted: user-installed modules are not keyed); `runs`, space-separated real paths of the programs the tool itself starts, granted execute and each keyed by its digest (perl's piped `open` of a command with a quote in it, as cryptogams' keccak1600-armv8.pl opens arm-xlate.pl, starts /bin/sh, which reads the link /private/var/select/sh and starts /bin/bash on this host); `needed_by`, the scripts' packages known to start it, space-separated, sorted. The tool's binary digest is in the run key and the record is marked `host-tool`: it never enters the shared cache. Read by blaze_build_script::host_tools.
